dossier.purpose: Python MCP server (stdio) plus a `ts` CLI/daemon. It builds an in-memory structural index of local project roots (symbols, imports, a name-based dependency graph) and serves it through 69 MCP tools: symbol lookup and source retrieval, dependents/impact, symbol-scoped edits (replace, insert, edit-lines, move, add-field), audits (dead code, breaking changes, config), git/test helpers, and a local SQLite persistent-memory engine. It also ships hook bundles (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenClaw) that compact Bash output. Definitions, references and edits come from its own annotators (Python ast, tree-sitter for Java/Ruby, regex/brace-counting for the other languages). Grep found no language-server client and no post-edit diagnostics feature in the repo.

claims.claim: Headline: 'One MCP server. One profile. 97.9% on tsbench at -80% tokens. Structural code navigation, persistent memory, and Bash output compaction for AI coding agents.'

96-task benchmark (Claude Opus 4.7, May 2026): plain Claude Code 141/180 (78.3%), 17,221 active tokens/task, 110.6 s/task vs Token Savior 188/192 (97.9%), 3,395 tokens (-80%), 18.9 s (-83%); reproduces with the 'optimized' profile.

Quick start: pip install token-savior-recall[mcp], then add an MCP entry whose command is the venv's token-savior binary with env WORKSPACE_ROOTS, TOKEN_SAVIOR_CLIENT and TOKEN_SAVIOR_PROFILE=optimized.
TOKEN_SAVIOR_PROFILE=optimized bundles tiny_plus (15 hot tools), thin inputSchema (-44% manifest), capture sandbox disabled, memory hooks gated for cross-project safety.

'It indexes your codebase by symbol -- functions, classes, imports, call graph -- so the model navigates by pointer instead of by cat. Measured reduction: 97% fewer chars injected across 170+ real sessions.'
Persistent memory engine: SQLite WAL + FTS5 + vector embeddings, ranked by Bayesian validity and ROI, re-injected as a compact delta at the start of the next session.
Profile table: optimized 15 tools (~1.5 KT, recommended), auto adaptive, tiny 6, lean 51, compact-only 1, full 68 (~6 KT).

Layers Token Savior owns that adjacent tools do not: the PreToolUse Bash rewriter, structural editing that keeps the index in sync, and the audit tools (detect_breaking_changes, find_dead_code, analyze_config).

On overlap with other tools, the README lists serena (symbol-graph navigation) as a direct overlap with find_symbol / get_dependents and advises running Token Savior as compact-only if serena is the navigator; running both is 'usually fine once you disable the half you already have'.

Token-savings table: find_symbol('send_message') 41M chars -> 67 chars (-99.9%); get_function_source('compile') 4.5K chars; get_change_impact('LLMClient') 16K chars ('impossible' without it); 96-task tsbench -80% active tokens.

`ts init --agent {claude,cursor,gemini,codex,openclaw}` deep-merges hook config (PostToolUse + PreToolUse), is idempotent, prints a diff and backs up settings.json; Bash compaction (34 compactors) and command rewriting (10 rules) are opt-in via TS_BASH_COMPACT=1 / TS_BASH_REWRITE=1.
`ts` CLI serves non-MCP agents (Cursor, Aider, Continue, scripts, CI) with a subset of tools; on Claude Code, prefer the MCP server ('measured cheaper than CLI on Opus 4.7').
Suite size: 1898 passed, 2 skipped on main. CI green on Python 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13.

code.architecture: Python package src/token_savior. Server: server.py builds the manifest from tool_schemas.py (69 tools), filters it by TOKEN_SAVIOR_PROFILE (server.py:431-452) and dispatches through four handler tables in server_handlers/ (META, MEMORY, SLOT, QFN; server_handlers/__init__.py:60-93), one call at a time under a global lock in a worker thread (server.py:1284-1333). Index: project_indexer.py walks files (defaults: 500 KB per file, 10,000 files, .gitignore plus vendor/build excludes; :201-244). annotator.py picks a per-language annotator by extension (python_annotator.py = ast; java_annotator.py and ruby_annotator.py = tree-sitter; typescript_, go_, rust_, csharp_, c_, php_, shell_annotator.py = regex plus brace_matcher.py; json/yaml/toml/ini/xml/hcl/dockerfile/prisma/gradle/env/conf/text annotators; generic_annotator.py = line-only fallback; annotator.py:28-137). It then builds a symbol table (first-found wins on duplicate names), an import graph and a name-based global/reverse dependency graph (project_indexer.py:717-747,1155-1307). query_api.py (3,154 lines) answers find_symbol, get_*_source, get_dependents, get_change_impact, get_full_context and search_codebase from that in-memory index. slot_manager.py keeps one index per root, refreshed by a watchfiles watcher or mtime polling (watcher.py), with a JSON cache `.token-savior-cache.json` in the project root (cache_ops.py:43). Edits: edit_ops.py plus server_handlers/edit.py splice by indexed line range and re-index the file; edit_verifier.py and workflow_ops.py (static EditSafety certificate, edit-then-run-impacted-tests) remain in the tree but are not registered as MCP tools (tests/test_tool_schemas.py:68-74). Other modules: memory/, memory_db.py and db_core.py (SQLite WAL + FTS5, optional sqlite-vec/fastembed), compactors/ and bash_rewriter/ (Bash output and command hooks), cli_init/ (hook installer), code_mode/ (Node vm worker), impacted_tests.py, breaking_changes.py, dead_code.py, config_analyzer.py (audits). Each MCP client spawns its own server process with its own in-memory index; edit handlers re-index the target file before writing to catch external changes (server_handlers/edit.py:16-43). No language-server client module exists.
code.packaging_and_release: Build backend hatchling (pyproject.toml:1-3). PyPI distribution name is token-savior-recall. The wheel packages only src/token_savior and force-includes hooks/ as token_savior/hooks (pyproject.toml:60-67). Release flow: when a GitHub Release is published, .github/workflows/publish.yml builds sdist and wheel with `python -m build` (:24-25), uploads dist/* to the release with `gh release upload` (:27-30) and uploads to PyPI with twine using a PYPI_API_TOKEN secret (:32-36). claim_checks.claim: It indexes your codebase by symbol -- functions, classes, imports, call graph -- so the model navigates by pointer (README.md:168-170).
claim_checks.evidence: Index and symbol tools exist (src/token_savior/annotator.py:28-97, project_indexer.py:717-747, query_api.py:1281-1323). It is a home-built index, not language-server data. Python uses stdlib ast and a name-only graph that records Name ids and the root of attribute chains (python_annotator.py:182-221). Java/Ruby use tree-sitter. TS/JS, Go, Rust, C#, C, PHP and shell use regex plus brace counting (typescript_annotator.py:1-8 says 'This is NOT a full TypeScript parser'; utils/dependency_graph.py:1-10). Cross-file edges come from word-boundary regex over bodies for imported names (project_indexer.py:1218-1287). get_dependents returns dependent symbols (definition file/line), not call-site positions, and a method query is widened to its class and sibling methods (query_api.py:1452-1486,3331-3344). Duplicate names resolve first-found-wins (project_indexer.py:721).

claim_checks.claim: Needs-driven check (the README makes no such claim): symbol definitions, references, edits or post-edit diagnostics are backed by language servers.
claim_checks.evidence: Repo-wide searches for language server / LSP / pyright / pylsp / tsserver / gopls / clangd / jedi / textDocument / publishDiagnostics found nothing (the only 'pyright' hit is the word 'Copyright' in LICENSE:3,12,18). No LSP library is in pyproject.toml:27-48. The only 'diagnostics' code is a Biome output compactor (compactors/biome.py:1). Post-edit feedback is limited to an '[EDIT IMPACT]' note listing callers and impacted tests (server.py:813-864,1078-1082); the EditSafety / edit-then-test workflow in workflow_ops.py has no MCP tool (tests/test_tool_schemas.py:68-74).

claim_checks.claim: Structural editing that keeps the index in sync (README.md:211-214; server.py:33-35).
claim_checks.evidence: Edit handlers re-index the target file before editing (server_handlers/edit.py:16-43) and after a successful write (edit.py:46-130). edit_ops.py splices by indexed line range with a root-containment check (edit_ops.py:11-63,130-214,217-248,344-380,436-565). replace_symbol_source keeps decorators/attributes (edit_ops.py:45-47,66-110). Caveats: move_symbol rewrites imports by regex only for .py/.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx (edit_ops.py:568-649); add_field_to_model supports only .prisma/.py/.ts/.tsx (edit_ops.py:390-404); no rename tool is exposed (tests/test_tool_schemas.py:68-74).

claim_checks.claim: TOKEN_SAVIOR_PROFILE=optimized exposes 15 hot tools, with the rest hidden behind ts_search; it bundles capture sandbox disabled and memory hooks gated (README.md:68-76,184-186; CLAUDE.md:15-19).
claim_checks.evidence: The 15-tool set is confirmed (server.py:337-361,445). The hidden tools are not discoverable through ts_search: _handle_ts_search scores only the advertised TOOLS (server.py:1160-1168; server_handlers/tool_search.py:255), and hidden tools run only if called by exact name (server.py:235-238). Not advertised under optimized: get_dependents, get_dependencies, get_change_impact, get_edit_context, get_class_source, insert_near_symbol, edit_lines_in_symbol, move_symbol; CLAUDE.md still routes to insert_near_symbol, move_symbol and find_import_cycles (CLAUDE.md:30-33). The code does not set TS_CAPTURE_DISABLED or TS_MEMORY_DISABLE for optimized (server.py:441-445,484-506), which matches README.md:332 but not the bundle bullets at README.md:68-74.

claim_checks.claim: Navigation returns the symbol's source directly ('get_function_source("compile") ... 4.5K chars ... direct', README.md:226) - 'exact source' retrieval.
claim_checks.evidence: Level 0 returns the full body (query_api.py:1164-1182). But when `level` is omitted, the handlers pick a level from a Thompson-sampling bandit persisted in the memory DB (server_handlers/code_nav.py:361-368; memory/lattice.py:71-109; it returns 0 only while all priors are untouched or on error), so signature, summary or name-only views (query_api.py:1217-1246) can be returned. Repeat reads of an unchanged symbol can return an 'unchanged' stub (code_nav.py:160-275). Classes over 300 lines default to a level-2 summary (query_api.py:1198-1210). get_full_context defaults to mode=compact: 80-line source head and dependents as names only (tool_schemas.py:463-467; code_nav.py:633-655). Passing level=0, force_full or mode=full returns the raw text.

risks: Not language-server based: definitions, references and edits rest on a heuristic index. TS/JS, Go, Rust, C#, C, PHP and shell are regex plus brace counting (src/token_savior/typescript_annotator.py:1-8; utils/dependency_graph.py:1-10); Python edges are name-based (python_annotator.py:182-221); get_dependents lists dependent symbols, not call sites, and widens a method to its class and siblings (query_api.py:1452-1486,3331-3344); get_change_impact 'confidence' is just 0.6^(depth-1) (query_api.py:1859); duplicate names are first-found-wins (project_indexer.py:721). No rename tool is exposed (tests/test_tool_schemas.py:68-74) and no compile/type/lint diagnostics run after an edit - only an '[EDIT IMPACT]' note with callers and impacted tests (server.py:813-864).

Default responses are not always the exact full text: with no `level`, get_function_source/get_class_source draw an abstraction level from a bandit persisted in the memory DB (server_handlers/code_nav.py:361-368; memory/lattice.py:71-109), so signature/summary/name-only views (query_api.py:1217-1246) can come back; repeat reads may return an 'unchanged' stub (code_nav.py:160-275); classes over 300 lines default to a summary (query_api.py:1198-1210); get_full_context defaults to an 80-line source head with dependents as names only (tool_schemas.py:463-467). Callers must pass level=0, force_full or mode=full.

The recommended `optimized` profile advertises only 15 tools (server.py:337-361,445). get_dependents, get_dependencies, get_change_impact, get_edit_context, get_class_source, insert_near_symbol, edit_lines_in_symbol and move_symbol are not in that manifest, and ts_search scores only advertised tools (server.py:1160-1168; server_handlers/tool_search.py:255), while CLAUDE.md routes to insert_near_symbol, move_symbol and find_import_cycles (CLAUDE.md:30-33). With TOKEN_SAVIOR_PROFILE unset the default is `full`, all 69 tools (server.py:144,458).

Claude Code footprint: `ts init --agent claude` edits ~/.claude/settings.json to add shell hooks on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, Stop and SessionEnd (hooks/memory-hooks-config.json:5-85; cli_init/agent_paths.py:148-154). Unless TS_MEMORY_DISABLE=1 they write user prompts (prompt_archive defaults to True; hooks/memory-userprompt.sh:218-271) and sandboxed tool outputs (memory_schema.sql:235,321) to ~/.local/share/token-savior/memory.db. Opt-in hooks: the Bash rewriter returns permissionDecision 'allow' with rewritten commands (hooks/bash_rewriter_hook.py:101-109); the discipline guard can deny native Read/Edit/Write/Grep on indexed source (hooks/ts_discipline_guard.py:41-43,346-359). A `.token-savior-cache.json` index file is written into every project root (cache_ops.py:43,54).

`ts_execute` runs model-supplied JavaScript in a long-lived Node worker whose `vm` context is seeded with the worker's own Object/Array/Promise/Error/etc. (src/token_savior/code_mode/worker.mjs:78-106). The subprocess inherits the full parent environment (code_mode/sandbox.py:131-138) and a grep of code_mode/ found no OS-level confinement. It is classed destructive (tool_annotations.py:58-68), exposed in full/auto/code_mode profiles, and removable with TS_CODE_MODE_DISABLE=1 (server.py:544-545). run_project_action and run_impacted_tests also run project commands via subprocess (project_actions.py:232-240; impacted_tests.py:171).

Documentation and packaging drift: README says 68 tools / 34 compactors / 1898 tests vs 69 / 42 / at least 2,728 in code and CHANGELOG (README.md:106,191,265; tests/test_tool_schemas.py:87; compactors/__init__.py:62-118; CHANGELOG.md:138). README's TS_SOCK default is /tmp/ts.sock vs the packaged CLI's per-user path (README.md:339; cli.py:52-66), while bin/ts still binds /tmp/ts.sock (bin/ts:51,231). `ts move` passes arguments the tool rejects (cli.py:591; tool_schemas.py:179-184). server.json says 4.19.0 (server.json:9,14) and uv.lock records 2.0.0 (uv.lock:1237-1238) vs 4.21.0 (pyproject.toml:7). The token-savior-bench script targets a module outside the wheel's packages (pyproject.toml:54,60-61). mypy strict is configured but never run (pyproject.toml:105-107).

Platform coverage beyond Linux is undocumented and untested: the README names no OS; CI is ubuntu-latest only (.github/workflows/ci.yml:11); shell hooks use GNU `stat -c` with `|| echo 0` fallbacks (hooks/memory-session-start.sh:30,64); the CLI daemon needs AF_UNIX sockets (src/token_savior/cli.py:131,268); CHANGELOG records Windows stderr problems (CHANGELOG.md:694-696). The optional embedding features need a first-use model download of about 130 MB via fastembed (ci.yml:45-46; memory/embeddings.py:31).

Process signals: the authors field lists one name (pyproject.toml:12-14); there is no SECURITY.md or dependabot config (.github/ holds workflows only); PyPI publishing uses a long-lived PYPI_API_TOKEN secret with no signing or attestation step (.github/workflows/publish.yml:32-36). CHANGELOG records a history rewrite to purge a leaked credential (CHANGELOG.md:671-675) and 'four hurried patch releases the same night' with 4.19.1 to 4.19.3 yanked (CHANGELOG.md:63-65). The latest stored in-repo retrieval result (semantic MRR@10 0.4759) sits below the repo's own CI gate of 0.65 (tests/benchmarks/code_retrieval/results/20260517-002528.md:13; scripts/check_bench_gates.py:29). The headline benchmarks are the author's own and live in an external repo (README.md:16-17,29).
